"It is therefore prayed that, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to set-aside /
quash the entire criminal proceedings pending in Criminal Case No.859/2021 J.P. Koshle vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11433095/
1 pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Baikunthpur, District - Korea (C.G.) against the present petitioner, in the interest of justice."

sentences.text: 3. Brief fact of the case is that on 05.04.2020, the complainant/ respondent No.2 lodged a report at Police Station, Sonhat, alleging therein that he belongs to scheduled tribe community and one agent namely Ashish Gupta of District Antyavasayi Sahakari Vikas Samiti Maryadit came to the house of complainant and asked him for obtaining loan saying that the complainant being the member of scheduled tribe may obtain loan for which he have to pay half loan amount.

As such Ashish Gupta lured the complainant to get the loan disbursed in his account after due formalities were fulfilled and in the year 2014 a cheque bearing No.311964 amounting to Rs.1,00,000/- was deposited in the bank account of complainant opened in Union Bank of India, Baikunthpur and Rs. 24,000/- cash was given to the complainant. Thereafter keeping the ATM card of the complainant, said Ashish Gupta has fraudulently withdrawn the total amount of Rs. 75,900/- through ATM of complainant on different dates and only cash Rs. 24,000/- was given to the complainant against the total loan amount of Rs. 1,00,000/-.

Being aggrieved by the forgery on 05.04.2020, the complainant/respondent No.2 has lodged FIR against the petitioner and Ashish Gupta for the offence punishable under Section 420, 34 of IPC at Police Station Sonhat, District Korea with Crime No.46/2020.
Upon due investigation, the charge sheet has been submitted before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Baikunthpur, District Korea.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Baikunthpur, District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present petitioner has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 16.12.2020.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that he has been falsely implicated in this case and if the case of prosecution is taken as it is then also the alleged offences are not made out against the petitioner.
The petitioner has not committed any fraud or cheating with the complainant.
At the relevant point of time, the petitioner was working in District Antyavasayi Sahakari Vikas Samiti Maryadit and he was authorized to sanction loan.

The complainant applied for loan before the said Samiti and after completion of formalities, the loan of Rs. 1,00,000/- was sanctioned in favour of complainant and the cheque of Rs. 1,00,000/- bearing cheque no. 311964 was issued to the complainant with the signature of petitioner and Collector and the said cheque was handed over to the complainant and thereafter the accused Ashish Gupta was having intention to commit cheating and fraud with the complainant since beginning and he has fraudulently withdrawn the amount from the bank account of complainant through ATM card, thus the cheating and fraud has been committed by Ashish Gupta and the present petitioner has no role to play fraud or cheating.

4. The learned counsel for the private respondent No.2 has submitted that there is no interim order passed in the present case and the case is fixed for framing of charge on 09.02.2022 and since the accused are not appearing and only his counsel is appearing, the charge could not be framed.
5.

It has been argued by the counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is posted as Chief Executive Officer in Cooperative Bank from where the loan of Rs.1,00,000/- was said to have been disbursed to the complainant and it is stated that the main allegation is against the co-accused Ashish Gupta who is said to have withdrawn the money of the complainant, out of which only Rs.24,000/- was given to him from the ATM.

The learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that FIR of the incident was lodged after six years and the applicant is being harassed in pursuance of the FIR and the charge sheet which have been submitted against him.

The counsel appearing on behalf of the J.P. Koshle vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11433095/
2 private respondent has vehemently opposed the prayer for quashing of the proceedings against the petitioner in the present case and has submitted that the petitioner along with Ashish Gupta had made fraud on him and has given him a cheque of Rs.1,00,000/- which was received by the complainant but ATM of the complainant was got deposited by Ashish Gupta whereby the money was withdrawn from the ATM and it has been further submitted that from the statement of the complainant recorded under 161 of CrPC with is annexed with the charge sheet which goes to show that the petitioner was also instrumental in getting the money withdrawn along with Ashish Gupta of the complainant and it is further submitted that the complainant because of the loan which he has taken, recovery proceedings have been initiated against him by the Tehsildar on 30.10.2024.

entities.text: J.P. Koshle vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: no ground for quashing rejected.
6. Learned State counsel has also pointed out that the accused are not appearing and only his counsel is appearing, the charge could not be framed.
7. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

8. The query has been made from the counsel for the petitioner as to why the accused are not appearing before the trial Court, he has not given the satisfactory reply, as such, we do not find any good ground to entertain this petition.
Accordingly, this petition is hereby dismissed.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Amitendra Kishore Prasad) (Ramesh Sinha)
